i. Volume of liquid corresponding to level L1 to L2 represents the solid vessel’s expansion (i.e. Vg = L1L2 × cross-section area) ii. Volume of liquid corresponding to level L1 to L3 represents an apparent expansion of liquid (i.e. Va = L1 L3× cross-section area) iii. Volume of liquid corresponding to level L2 to L3 represents the real expansion of liquid (i.e. Vr = L2L3 × cross-section area)

There are different coefficients of expansion; coefficient of real expansion, coefficient of apparent expansion, and coefficient of volume expansion of glass vessel which are defined as follows. Coefficient of real expansion of liquid: The real change in volume of liquid per unit original volume per unit rise in temperature is called the coefficient of real expansion of liquid. It is denoted as r and is given by; r = Real change in volume of liquid (Vr ) Original volume of liquid (V0 )  Change in temperature (θ) or, r = ΔVr . . . (1) [Where,  = 2 – 1] V0Δθ

Coefficient of apparent expansion of liquid: The apparent change in the volume of liquid per unit original volume per unit change in temperature is called the coefficient of apparent expansion of liquid. It is denoted by a and is given by; a = Apparent change in volume of liquid (Va ) Original volume of liquid (V0 )  Change in temperature (θ) or, a = ΔVa . . . (2), V0Δθ
Coefficient of volume expansion of solid: The change in volume of glass vessel per unit
original volume per unit rise in temperature is called the coefficient of volume expansion of
glass vessel. It is denoted by g and given by;
g = Change in volume of solid vessel(Vg ) Original volume of solid vessel(V0 )  Change in temperature (θ)
